Dear, good [old slave](/person/113),
How nice and kind and understanding your letter was, and how thankful one should be for such friends! ...
The worst will be over when we hear from [Julian](/person/1624), poor boy! Till then it seems like bearing the first stroke. But I am sure it fell mercifully as far as we were concerned, and the flow of feelings that meet us from all is very gratifying.
I believe [my uncle](/person/1614), always living in his own town far off, had no notion of the estimation in which his brother was held.
. . . I know I shall miss [him](/person/1631) more when he has been away longer.
